story.head: Second night of a back-to-back for the Sabres
paras: The Canucks are on a three-game losing streak, and the Sabres (11-11-4) lost 6-3 to Pittsburgh on Nov 27. The Sabres played last night, and the Canucks are rested. Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Sabres’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth. The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.232) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .343, and their goaltending has held them back.
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 89-81, even though they’ve outscored teams 57-55 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 25-15.

The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). The Canucks pick their shots (lowest), have had shaky goaltending (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (32nd). Vancouver has allowed 4.43 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one. Beyond that, the Canucks roll four lines, but the Sabres lean on their top six.

Tage Thompson (17 G / 14 A / 31 P in 26 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (14 G / 12 A / 26 P in 26 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. For the Canucks, Brock Boeser (8 G / 20 A / 28 P in 28 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jake DeBrusk (9 G / 6 A / 15 P in 26 GP) has a team-high nine goals.
Alex Lyon (0-3-1 / .896 SV% in 4 GS) will likely start for Buffalo, and Leevi Meriläinen (4-12-1 / .883 SV% in 18 GS) for Vancouver.
The Sabres usually control more of the chances than the Canucks do.

items.text: Luke Schenn faces his old team, Buffalo.
The Sabres are newly without Zach Benson and Noah Östlund, and have been without Konsta Helenius since Oct 27.
The Canucks are newly without Filip Chytil, have been without Elias Pettersson (#40) since Nov 19, and have had to make do without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
Tage Thompson has scored in three straight games against Vancouver.
